summary: Introductory discovery call between Redwood AE/SE and Ironclad Integrations to scope a channel integration and a short pilot. Discussed integration models (hosted API vs dedicated vs private/VPC), security requirements (SOC2/SSO/KMS), performance expectations (p99 latency, batching, KV/prefix cache), and commercial considerations for reseller margins. Agreed on a 2-week pilot with reserved capacity and a follow-up technical deep dive for private deployment. Action items assigned.
topics: Deployment options: hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC
Performance: latency SLOs, batching, KV cache
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-01-08 16:00 PST — Duration 47 mins. Attendees: Sophie Kim (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nora Patel (Redwood Solutions), Markus Vetter (Ironclad CTO), Aisha Patel (Ironclad Head of Cloud), Ravi Singh (Infra), Ellen Cho (Procurement).

Summary: quick partner intro, scope pilot and technical constraints, initial ask for security docs and pilot parameters.

00:00 Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Sophie from Redwood. Quick round robin?
00:12 Markus: Markus here, CTO at Ironclad Integrations. We're the SI that builds hybrid inference stacks for finance and healthcare.
00:18 Aisha: Aisha, run cloud team, we manage deployments and security for partner integrations.
00:24 Sophie: Awesome. Diego, do you want to intro the technical bits?
00:28 Diego: Yeah hi, Diego Alvarez, solution engineer. I'll focus on latency/cost tradeoffs, deployment patterns, and what we normally ship for channel partners.
00:32 Markus: Cool. High level — we're exploring a reseller model where we bundle Redwood inference into our managed offering and sometimes run private for customers with strict data rules.
00:40 Sophie: Got it. So two things to cover: the channel economics (margins/contracting) and the technical integration for both hosted and private modes.
00:48 Ellen: From procurement side I'm mostly curious about contract length, pilot terms and how billing looks when we resell.
00:55 Nora: We can do reserved capacity rollups for Dedicated and an enterprise contract for Private. For hosted we do usage billing.
01:05 Ravi: Technical constraints — many of our customers require VPC peering or on-prem options and KMS integration. Also strict egress controls.
01:12 Diego: Totally expected. For private deployments we offer a customer-controlled control plane and we can integrate with your KMS/HSM for key wrapping. For VPC we normally do peering and have port lists and NAT egress controls. We'll share network diagrams.
01:25 Aisha: What's the difference in latency between hosted and dedicated? Our customers are latency sensitive — p99 under 300ms for short prompts.
01:33 Diego: There's a few moving parts. Hosted on our multi-tenant pool typically has higher variance — p95 is good, p99 can spike under load. Dedicated reserved pools are much more predictable. With batching and prefix caching you can often reduce per-token cost and keep p99 tighter. For short sequences you should see sub-300ms p99 on Dedicated for the smaller models; larger models depend on sequence length and quantization.
01:55 Markus: Can you explain prefix cache — we heard KV cache and prefix caching terms and I worry about coherence across our sessions.
02:02 Diego: Sure. We have automatic prefix/K V cache (sometimes transcribed as K V cash) — it stores KV states for recent prompts to reduce recomputation. It can be per-customer or shared depending on privacy needs. For private it's per-customer/namespace; for hosted we have tenancy isolation. The cache is managed by the runtime and has TTL and size controls.
02:25 Markus: Ok that helps. On security — SOC2, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, can we get that stuff?
02:31 Sophie: Yes. We'll share SOC2 docs and our security brief. We support SAML SSO, OIDC, RBAC at the tenant level, and audit logs with retention tiers. KMS integrations are via customer-managed keys in Private deployments.
02:43 Aisha: How mature is the on-prem package? Some of our regulated customers require an air-gapped install.
02:50 Diego: We have an on-prem bundle used by a few finance customers. It requires an initial control-plane handshake; for air-gapped we provide an offline installer and audit guidance. There are some manual steps for kernel selection and GPU driver tuning — we usually do a workshop for the first install.
03:05 Markus: Great. For the reseller model, do you allow us to rebrand API endpoints or do calls need to show Redwood?
03:11 Sophie: We support white-labeling for channel partners under enterprise terms— there are branding and contract considerations. Billing can be handled either as pass-through or via a reseller agreement. We'll share a commercial note.
03:20 Ellen: Margin targets — we typically need 20-30% to make it viable. How flexible on partner pricing?
03:26 Sophie: We can explore partner-tier pricing for committed reserved capacity. For pilot and PoC it's usually usage-based. If you commit to a certain reserved committed level we can provide tiered discounts.
03:35 Aisha: Pilot scope — we want to validate p99 and throughput for a reranking pipeline and a short-chat use case. Any recommendations on token profiles?
03:43 Diego: For reranking include high token bursts — e.g., 2k tokens per call at 100 qps for a short window — and for chat typical 30-150 tokens. We'll want to test end-to-end including network egress, batching, and prefix hits. We'll propose a perf test plan.
04:00 Markus: Network — what ports and peering setup do you need?
04:05 Diego: We'll send a lightweight network checklist. Usually outbound HTTPS to control plane plus a few TCP ports for GRPC to the inference nodes if using private peering. For Dedicated we do tenant-isolated routing.
04:15 Aisha: Data residency — some EU customers require data to never leave region. Do you have region locks?
04:20 Sophie: Yes, we support region pinning and can deploy Dedicated or Private within EU regions. For hosted we have region options; for strict residency we recommend Private.
04:30 Ravi: I'm worried about model versions and rollback — we need pinning and A/B rollouts to avoid regressions.
04:35 Diego: Rollouts are first-class — canary deploys, A/B splits, automatic fallback policies. We also tie regressions to eval sets and can block rollouts if quality drops.
04:46 Markus: For pilot, what's the minimum reserved capacity we should start with?
04:50 Diego: For the pilot you could start with 2 reserved GPUs (NVIDIA A10/A30 class equivalent) for 2 weeks, run synthetic and real traffic. We'll size based on your token profile; the test plan will have a recommended capacity.
04:59 Ellen: Procurement timeline? We can get pilot approvals in 2 weeks if terms are simple.
05:03 Sophie: Sounds workable. We'll aim to get the SOC2 and network diagram over today/tomorrow.
05:08 Aisha: Can we do a technical deep-dive next week focused on private deployment steps and driver tuning?
05:13 Diego: Yes let's schedule. I'd like Ravi to join to walk through infra diagrams.
05:18 Markus: Any concerns about licensing for quantized models — some vendors limit redistribution?
05:23 Diego: Good point. Model licensing varies. For some open models we can host them; for vendor-licensed models there may be specific redistribution terms. We usually keep model catalog metadata tied to each model and can enforce policy.
05:36 Nora: Quick note on observability: Redwood Console can show per-route token breakdown, p99 latency, trace hooks and error analysis. You can also export traces into your SRE pipelines.
05:47 Ravi: Is there a way to run local benchmarks against your runtime image before deploying?
05:52 Diego: We provide a reference image and a small benchmark harness. For Private installs we run calibration scripts during the onboarding workshop. For hosted we can run a synthetic load against a sandbox.
06:05 Sophie: Any final procurement or compliance questions?
06:10 Ellen: We'll need the standard security questionnaire answered. Also want to confirm the pilot is non-binding and we can opt out after two weeks.
06:17 Sophie: Pilot will be non-binding; we'll send a short pilot SOW.
06:22 Markus: OK — recap?
06:25 Sophie: Recap: Redwood to send SOC2 and security brief, network checklist, and a perf test plan. Ironclad to share infra diagrams and procurement timing. Agreed pilot: 2 reserved GPUs for two weeks to validate p99 and throughput, followed by technical deep dive for private deployment.
06:40 Aisha: Sounds good. Thanks all.
06:44 Sophie: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the docs and schedule. Bye.

Action items listed above. Questions asked during call included: how caching works, latency differences, on-prem air-gap process, reseller billing/resale options, model licensing constraints.
